newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee appreciation around 14 pct - RBI.
newsitem.headline: India rupee appreciation around 14 pct - RBI.

text.p: The appreciation of the Indian rupee in real effective terms is around 14 percent at present, as compared with March 1993, a senior official of the country's central bank said on Friday.

"Presently, compared to March 1993, the appreciation of the Indian rupee in real effective terms is around 14 percent," Deputy Governor Y.V. Reddy of the Reserve Bank of India told a meeting of forex dealers in the resort state of Goa.

Reddy said the Indian economy has certain favourable factors in terms of a moderate CAD/GDP ratio, high foreign exchange reserves and a much lower ratio of short-term debt to reserves than that of the East Asian countries.

"Our inflation rate is also edging downwards," he added. "We have a fairly solid banking system despite the non-performing assets; the number of non-bank financial companies is not that large; and the financial sector is subject to reasonably effective regulation by the RBI."
Reddy said these factors combined to make India's financial sector less vulnerable than many of the East Asian economies, even despite the fact that many corporates operate with unhedged positions.
